channel.description: Latest articles from The Chronicle of Higher Education (chronicle.com)

item.title: ‘A Painful Reckoning’: After Bombshell Report, Higher Ed Scrambles to Review Cesar Chavez Tributes
item.description: By Kate Hidalgo Bellows The New York Times reported Wednesday that the labor-rights activist sexually abused and groomed girls for years. Many colleges host programs, statues, and other markers of his legacy.

item.title: Hundreds of Colleges and Professors Implore Ed. Dept. to Reverse 'Dangerous' Changes for Grad Students
item.description: By Taylor Swaak In a Chronicle analysis of public comments submitted to the Trump administration, key themes emerged.

item.title: States Are Demanding Curricular Changes. How Are Colleges Responding?
item.description: By Jasper Smith The University of Wyoming’s president recently faced an ambiguous demand: expel “institutional discrimination” from the curriculum.

item.title: Utah Lawmakers Pass Law Exempting Speakers From Anti-DEI Law
item.description: Explore where college diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts are under attack.By Chronicle StaffLegislators want to get rid of DEI offices, end diversity trainings, banish diversity statements, and censor how professors talk about race, gender, and sexuality in mandatory courses.

item.title: Can Danielle Allen Save Academe From Itself?
item.description: The Harvard political theorist is the sector's most interesting reformer. By Charlie Tyson The Harvard political theorist is the sector's most interesting reformer.

item.title: When Faculty Stop Showing Up
item.description: Faculty disengagement is reshaping campus life, one closed door at a time.By David DeMatthews Faculty disengagement is reshaping campus life, one closed door at a time.

item.title: Economic Affirmative Action Is Working
item.description: Low-income students are the beneficiaries of the Supreme Court’s striking down race-conscious admissions.By Richard D. Kahlenberg Low-income students are the beneficiaries of the Supreme Court's striking down race-conscious admissions.

item.title: U. of Kansas Faculty and Students Voted No Confidence in the Chancellor. Or Did They?
item.description: By Megan Zahneis Upset by leaders' handling of campus finances, students and faculty overwhelmingly panned them in a straw poll. But the university says the survey was unscientific, skewed, and aimed at a predetermined result.

item.title: AI Broke College Assessment. One University Believes It's Got a Fix.
item.description: By Emmy Martin The University of Sydney, in Australia, created a menu of assignment options for instructors — and now effectively allows students to use AI tools for most work outside the classroom.

item.title: After Settlement and Fine, Cornell Faces Another Federal Investigation
item.description: The federal government is reshaping its relationship with the nation's colleges. Here's the latest.By Chronicle Staff The Chronicle is tracking executive orders, statements from Trump, and agency actions that affect higher education, plus legal challenges directed at those measures. Here’s the latest.

item.title: In the Classroom, Efficiency Isn't Everything
item.description: Good pedagogy isn't streamlined. It's ritualistic and sacrificial.By Alan Levinovitz Good pedagogy isn't streamlined. It's ritualistic and sacrificial.

item.title: Elise Stefanik Goes Woke
item.description: The crusading politician's book about higher ed embodies everything she says she's against.By Alex Bronzini-Vender The crusading politician's book about higher ed embodies everything she says she's against.

item.title: Can You Hang a Pride Flag in Your Office Window? This University Says No.
item.description: By Emma Pettit Boston University has drawn a line between personal and institutional speech. Some professors see censorship.
